checks: Verified original 891aaf58ec0549c1 at its declared digest, opening (1)–(2), §1 and §2 through (5). The retained result is the exact fixed-mass characterization and attainment, independent of the supplementary §3 estimates.

The normalization divides both measures by |B| and preserves the centroid. The accepted argument gives the very same scalar constraints at a parallel through-centroid cap. Its proof uses the centroid under κ+2ν even though its final cap bound is about κ+ν. Monotonicity under containment gives the stated lower bound for the weighted mass κ+2ν on arbitrary containing halfspaces.

At s=1 the mass constraints force r=α and the Jensen slack is (q−1)+2α(q−α^(1/d))>0. At s=0 one has r=0 and the right side is 1+2α^q>0. The continuous inequality and mass constraints define a compact nonempty domain.

At strict slack with r>0 a common small decrease of s and r preserves s−r and s+α−r, and all bounds persist. With r=0 the one-coordinate decrease preserves both mass constraints. In each case the objective strictly drops. This excludes strict slack and therefore excludes s=1 for every minimizer.

On the volume-one simplex the cap at barycentric threshold t is a homothety of ratio 1−t, so v=(1−X)^d is uniform including d=1. The two rank bands are legal, have total length α, intersect at most at a null boundary, and capture exactly r at the prospective cap. Integrating v^(1/d) on each band gives the numerator used in the centroid formula; saturation makes the actual projected centroid 1−s^(1/d). The cutting boundary passes through the full centroid because the coordinate is affine.
At α=0, r=0; at α=1, both r≤s and s≤r force r=s. In either case the constraint reduces to q s^(q−1)≥1, the objective is s, and q^(−d) is feasible and minimal.
